title: New vowel, new word
goal: Blend a CVC word with a newly taught vowel and read it in a controlled sentence.
evidence: Listen for /d/ /o/ /g/ blended as dog and accurate reading of the sentence; note audio support.
lesson: After explicit teaching of short o; transfer to dot or got on paper.

title: Two letters, one sound
goal: Read sh as one sound and blend it with other taught correspondences.
evidence: Student blends shop without separating s and h, then reads Sam sat in a shop.; check a different sh word.
lesson: After teaching sh; use ship as the next independent word.

title: The shrinking puddle
goal: Explain evaporation and predict how shade could affect a puddle under otherwise similar conditions.
evidence: Diagram and narration link liquid water to water vapour in air; prediction has a reason and recognises other conditions.
lesson: After observing puddles or modelling changes of state; discuss what the diagram cannot show.

title: Change the pivot
goal: Use a lever model to explain how pivot position affects the effort required for the same load.
evidence: Student relates distances from the pivot to the load and effort and provides a consistent diagram/narration.
lesson: Consolidation after a physical lever demonstration; predict before testing.

title: Shade or a smoother path?
goal: Recommend a council project within a budget while addressing competing access and comfort needs.
evidence: Choice cites both resident views, calculates remaining funds and acknowledges a trade-off.
lesson: Apply agreed decision criteria after learning about local services.

title: A service beyond the trial
goal: Distinguish a funded trial from an ongoing commitment and justify a decision under uncertainty.
evidence: Student cites trial costs, access needs and unknown future funding; identifies information needed.
lesson: Later civics lesson on recurring costs and evaluating proposals.

title: Weather at one spot
goal: Record a temperature comparison with consistent method and separate measured change from explanation.
evidence: Student uses units, time and location, identifies a measured difference and proposes a further observation.
lesson: Outdoor weather mission followed by a short classroom comparison.

title: A puddle after rain
goal: Use repeated observations of one location to describe change while recognising limits of the measurement.
evidence: Student distinguishes a shorter puddle from a measured volume loss and proposes a way to improve evidence.
lesson: After rainfall observation; revisit safely with teacher and compare class records.

title: Keeping water warm
goal: Interpret controlled cooling data and distinguish evidence from a general claim about materials.
evidence: Student uses the temperature change or final temperatures, identifies controlled conditions and suggests repeats.
lesson: After predicting which wrapping will reduce cooling; compare with a supervised physical test if suitable.

title: Plan a dissolving test
goal: Design a fair test by changing water temperature while controlling relevant quantities and method.
evidence: Student specifies temperature as independent variable, consistent sugar/water/stirring and a measurable end point.
lesson: Planning phase before simulation; discuss predictions before running.

title: A smaller batch
goal: Halve every ingredient in a recipe while preserving proportions.
evidence: Student halves all three quantities consistently and explains the operation.
lesson: After physical halving; check the same reasoning with a different recipe.

title: Share the muffins
goal: Represent equal sharing and explain the link between total, groups and group size.
evidence: Student distributes 12 muffins among 4 plates equally and explains how they know shares are equal.
lesson: Small-group division task; repeat with counters off screen.

title: The fallen tower
goal: Retell a pictured event with a clear beginning, change and resolution.
evidence: Recording identifies people, event order and a reason connecting the problem to response; revision improves one unclear point.
lesson: Oral language small group after teacher models sequencing words.

title: A lunchbox mix-up
goal: Describe people and objects precisely enough for a listener to follow a story.
evidence: Student distinguishes two similar objects using relevant detail and clarifies ambiguous pronouns.
lesson: EAL/D or oral-language lesson on description and reference.

title: Map the reading room
goal: Use a key and grid references to locate landmarks and create directions another person can follow.
evidence: Partner follows directions from A3 to C1, with landmarks named consistently; student revises ambiguity.
lesson: After walking a school room and discussing bird’s-eye maps.

title: Choose useful map symbols
goal: Create a consistent map key and use it to explain the location of a landmark.
evidence: Student matches each symbol to one place and describes relative position using the map.
lesson: Map-making phase before exchanging navigation challenges.

title: Before the rain
goal: Make a plausible prediction supported by more than one textual clue.
evidence: Prediction connects clouds and preparations, acknowledges that the future event is not certain.
lesson: Pause-before-reading-on activity in a comprehension lesson.

title: The missing class plant
goal: Reconcile apparently conflicting statements by considering sequence and limits of knowledge.
evidence: Student uses yesterday/today timing and the pot clue to propose a coherent explanation without accusing a character.
lesson: Later comprehension task on contradictions and revised inference.

title: A quiet place to work
goal: Explore how differing sensory and activity needs can be accommodated through discussion.
evidence: Student asks rather than assumes what each person needs, proposes an adjustment and considers both effects.
lesson: Class discussion before group work; adult supports any needed accommodation.

title: A change to the game
goal: Discuss fairness when rules change and propose a response that considers different perspectives.
evidence: Student explains both concerns, predicts consequences and revises a proposal after hearing another view.
lesson: Teacher-facilitated social problem-solving before playground role-play.

title: Name the destination
goal: Replace an ambiguous reference with a precise noun or location and verify the result.
evidence: Student specifies the intended red flag rather than an unclear it and explains how the change resolves ambiguity.
lesson: Procedural writing mini-lesson on precise references.

title: Put the steps in order
goal: Sequence procedural actions so that each required condition is met before the next action.
evidence: Student places pickup before delivery and describes why the original order cannot work.
lesson: Writing directions lesson; test a revised sequence with a partner.

title: A precise description
goal: Revise vague wording with relevant detail drawn from the writer’s own notes.
evidence: Student adds informative detail, preserves the intended event and explains how it helps a reader.
lesson: Focused revision after drafting; teacher assigns description as the single goal.

title: Clarify who did what
goal: Resolve an ambiguous reference while preserving the writer’s intended meaning.
evidence: Student replaces or clarifies an unclear pronoun and explains how the reader can identify the actor.
lesson: Revision lesson on cohesion after students have drafted a short recount.
